findings.summary: AC-02 (acceptance.md:41-53) and T-02 (tasks.md:13) have no pre-execution baseline; git status --porcelain already falsifies both before T-01 runs (modified changes/medium/*, untracked changes/.transactions/, changes/high/lanes/, changes/high/reviews/, changes/high/specs/, changes/medium/lanes/, changes/medium/reviews/). A gate that is red for unrelated reasons pushes an implementer to revert changes/medium/ to make it green.

D-04 (design.md:138-142,174-176) justifies silent fall-through on unknown arguments on the grounds that no check pins it, then pins it twice: spec.md:22-26 makes it a normative SHALL that spec archive merges into specs/cli-output/, and acceptance.md:77-81 makes it a required criterion with task T-03. Adding strictness later would then be a breaking MODIFIED requirement, which is exactly what D-04 claimed to avoid.

D-02's rationale (design.md:116-119) is factually false: Array.prototype.includes compares elements exactly, so a directory path containing the substring --json never equals '--json'. The derived delta-spec scenario spec.md:51-56 is unfalsifiable and the requirement spec.md:46-50 promotes a false premise into a durable spec. The slice(2) decision itself is correct, for the honest reason that argv[0..1] are not user arguments.
spec.md:40-44 asserts source structure ('because both read one constant in the source') as observable behavior; the causal clause belongs in D-03, not in a spec scenario.

includes scans every user argument, so 'node cli.mjs somefile --json' selects JSON and the POSIX '--' separator is not honored. Acceptable for a two-vector CLI, but should be a stated knowing acceptance.

design.md:253-254 claims the writable set is exactly cli.mjs plus changes/high/**, while design.md:248 lists changes/.transactions/ as Do-Not-Touch even though the my-flow tooling writes there during this change (also changes/high/reviews/, changes/high/lanes/, .my-flow/). As phrased it generates false violations at T-02.
